Samantha - this is excellent, thanks for the detail. Sketching out model of costs and next steps below based on your profile. I attached a preliminary estimate PDF (redwood-pricing-estimate-acme-q2.pdf).

Pricing sketch (illustrative; final = after signed MSA/commit):
- Pricing tiers (committed monthly tokens):
  - 0-5M: $700 per 1M tokens
  - 5-25M: $400 per 1M tokens
  - 25M+: $300 per 1M tokens
- Context-length uplift guidance (example):
  - 8k baseline: standard tier price
  - 32k: +20% per-1M uplift (memory + batch inefficiencies)
  - 128k: +80% per-1M uplift (higher memory and scheduling cost)

Example cost (mix from your profile, mid-ramp 25M):
- Mix: 60% 8k / 30% 32k / 10% 128k => effective multiplier ~1.17 vs baseline
- Baseline price at 25M tier: $300 per 1M => raw = $300 * 25 = $7,500
- Add context uplift (~17%): ~$1,275 => estimated monthly = $8,775

This puts you within your target band for committed pricing if you hit ~25M/mo. For pilot volumes (1-2M) estimated price per 1M is higher (see 0-5M tier). We can propose a short-term pilot discount to get you started while you ramp.

Dedicated / reserved capacity: yes - reserved GPU pools can lower the per-token unit at scale because of predictable utilization. If you're open to commit-level pricing (6-12 month), we can move to a deeper discount and a flat $/1M target in the $250-350 range depending on commit and SLA.

Next steps:
1) Confirm which tier you expect to commit to for the first 6 months (pilot vs ramp).
2) If you want a technical deep-dive on 32k/128k performance, Jordan suggested a 30-min session.
3) Procurement: if you want a draft MSA/SOW we'll route to legal after we lock volumes.

Attachment: redwood-pricing-estimate-acme-q2.pdf

Best,

Marissa / Samantha - quick technical note to clarify how context length impacts unit economics and operational choices.

On Wed, May 12, 2027 at 3:10 PM Samantha Liu <samantha.liu@acme.com> wrote:
> 3) Context length distribution (estimated):
> - 8k: ~60%
> - 32k: ~30%
> - 128k: ~10%

Short take: those distributions are realistic and we have two levers that materially affect price and performance:
1) Model variant & quantization: using optimized quantized models (int8 / 4-bit) reduces GPU memory and can reduce cost by ~10-30% depending on workload quality tolerance.
2) Serving mode (hosted shared vs dedicated): Dedicated pools give predictable throughput and allow better packing/long-context strategies, which reduces effective per-token cost for 32k/128k by reducing idle memory overhead.

Approx uplift factors we use for quick planning (back-of-envelope):
- 8k baseline = x1.0
- 32k = x1.20 (roughly +20%)
- 128k = x1.80 (roughly +80%)

If you want to approximate final bid price: apply tiered price then multiply by uplift factor by percentage of tokens at each context length.

Recommended next step: 30-min technical deep-dive where we review a 10-20 sample documents you shared (we can use the CSV) and run a quick profile that outputs an expected average prompt/completion breakdown and a more precise cost model. I can join Friday morning (PST) or Monday.

- Jordan
